judgment: UCR supplies genuine biomedical foundations (cell biology, physiology, biochemistry, pharmacology, infection/immunity and pathology), laboratory methods, epidemiology, health psychology and statistics. Those contributions do not establish a substantive programme response to dentistry. ACTA combines sustained oral biology/cariology/periodontology, direct and indirect restorations, endodontology, dental care planning and medically complex patient study with 62EC of named dental skills/prevention-treatment/radiology lines, plus the14EC dental research placement. UCR has no taught course in these defining dental subjects or dental clinical/manual techniques. Functional Anatomy explicitly offers academic learning, not clinical skills; its named regions do not establish dental-arch/occlusion teaching. Mechanisms of Disease covers cardiovascular,lung,kidney,digestive,endocrine andCNS systems, not a caries course. Psychodiagnostics concerns mental-health assessment/psychotherapy, not oral diagnosis. Rhetoric with schoolchildren, general leadership, civil-society sociology, environmental justice and public economics cannot supply missing dental treatment, oral-health service design or patient-care competencies. First proposal has11biomedical/publichealth/lab courses82.5EC plus psychology/methods/rhetoric/law/PPD; the second has only4biomedical/publichealth courses30EC plus psychology and social/policy companions. Whole7.5EC course contributions are credited as actually taught, not relabelled as dentistry. Biomedical science/health equity can be coherent UCR programmes but address different targets; diversification cannot repair absent dental substance. This judgment is about academic content and weight, independently of professional licensing or direct master admission. Full151course workbook search for dental/orofacial/cariology/periodontal/endodontic/restorative/oralhealth terminology found no defining specialist course, and all35selected profiles were read. No defensible alternative or invented schedule retained.
